project.name: Elliot
project.boundarySource: Mapped named-place location with a conservative editorial study buffer
project.researchNotes: Full sequential audit. Elliot remains 30 and selector-only: the coast route is published separately and West Links/Elliot Beach facilities remain with Arbroath. No public bunker access, cafe-led Eat, dedicated picnic site, local public car park or public toilet was verified inside the strict hamlet boundary. All 12 HES/NRHE records remain; eight visible pins have defensible material dates and four period-unassigned records are map-hidden. Angus-wide full audit completed 2026-09-01: all six visitor categories, the four named commercial trail providers, current official/conventional routes, strict-boundary scoring and local HES/NRHE integrity were checked.

touristAppeal.label: Minor Interest
touristAppeal.summary: A small coastal-edge hamlet and route waypoint without an independently visitable centre or visitor-service cluster. Elliot Beach and West Links facilities belong to Arbroath and are not transferred into this score.
touristAppeal.dogAccessSummary: The coast route can suit controlled dog walking, but tide, burn crossings, wildlife, roads and neighbouring beach rules need checking.

townGuide.headline: A waypoint, not a standalone visitor town
townGuide.intro: Elliot scores 30% and stays in the selector but off the town map. The official Arbroath–Carnoustie coast route passes the locality, while West Links Beach, its picnic ground, parking, toilets and café are correctly retained under Arbroath rather than borrowed by Elliot.

features.shortDescription: ELLIOT, NORTH OF  A92, FORMER ROYAL OBSERVER CORPS UNDERGROUND MONITORING POST
features.reviewNotes: Material date Built 1958; designation and database dates were not used. NRHE record linked by matching point location; review if it represents a distinct asset.
features.fullDescription: 1958. Underground rectangular bunker with 2 internal chambers, accessed via metal ladder in narrow entrance shaft and with ventilation and detecting structures above ground. Reinforced concrete. ABOVE GROUND: low, square-plan green painted concrete entrance hatch on concrete plinth with base course and bevelled top edge. Concrete step to E. Square-plan ventilation shaft with louvred openings to N. Top opening metal entrance door leads to vertical shaft with wall mounted metal ladder, leading to bunker. To W: low, capped louvred ventilation shaft. Cylindrical survey meter probe cover and bomb power indicator baffle plates. INTERIOR: large rectangular plan monitoring room with smaller rectangular ancillary room. Smaller chamber with toilet. Timber door with moulded surround with vent to bottom leads to large monitoring room with rubber flooring and small metal piles leading to external recording meters. Some timber moulding surrounding notice board and wall mounted timber desk. Some surviving wall mounted communication equipment. Iron grill to floor below ladder.
